startup.name: Smartbase
startup.description: An ERP built around AI for small and mid sized manufacturers, covering inventory, production planning, purchasing and finance, sold as a subscription that replaces legacy ERP and spreadsheets. Description in the input is a single sentence.

yc_acceptance.basis: YC publishes no acceptance rate; the working prior is about 1 percent with a band of 0.6 to 2 percent (references/yc_acceptance.md). This company is already in the batch named in the input, so the number is for completeness only. Two founders and a one sentence description with no traction; ERP for manufacturers is a real, large, painful market but a well worn one, so about 1.2 percent. Already in the batch.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: ERP is a huge schlep with long sales cycles and a rewrite risk, and a one sentence pitch with two founders gives no evidence of manufacturing domain knowledge or customers. YC may also ask why this succeeds where several recent AI ERP entrants and Recurrency style companies are already active.

narrative.headline: An ambitious ERP with a short 7 month window means a low seed chance by construction, close to cohort anchors.
narrative.general_summary: Smartbase is an AI native ERP for manufacturers with two founders and a one line description. The window is only 7.4 months, shorter than the median 8 months to seed in the B2B cohort, so about 22 percent is the honest estimate with no lift for AI. These numbers do not rank it against other companies; they reflect timing and the slow, schlep heavy category. ERP for manufacturers is a large, painful market, but the input is a single sentence. The scored numbers are window specific and anchored on older cohorts, and the remaining risk is mostly execution and timing rather than the idea alone.
